stories.title: Trump: 'We don't need a deal with Iran'
stories.body: President Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran and told Vice-President Vance, who had led negotiations, to focus on domestic issues. Secretary of State Rubio said economic pressure on Iran is working and will get worse, so large-scale military operations are unnecessary. Iran says it has sent a seven-condition proposal through Qatar and that the ball is in the US court. On the same day, Iran claimed it struck a US radar site in Bahrain; the US said it shot down two Iranian drones and nothing was damaged.
stories.why: A long 'no war, no peace' stand-off keeps Hormuz disrupted and oil prices high, which shapes Nigeria's revenue and fuel costs.

cards.front: How did Chatham House describe the US–Iran situation in November 2026?
cards.back: "No war, no peace": neither a deal nor full-scale fighting.

stories.title: Abu Dhabi talks end with a large prisoner swap deal
stories.body: Two days of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi ended with Russia and Ukraine agreeing a large-scale prisoner exchange, but no breakthrough on ending the war. US envoy Jared Kushner called it a tough but productive meeting and said territory remains the hardest issue, with progress on a post-war security framework. Ukraine's negotiator David Arakhamia spoke of good momentum and said the next talks should include more parties.
stories.why: Each round of talks moves the chance of a ceasefire that would ease world food and fuel prices.

cards.front: What was agreed at the Abu Dhabi talks of 10–11 November 2026?
cards.back: A large-scale prisoner exchange; no deal on ending the war.

stories.title: Nigeria's inflation eases to 14.63 percent
stories.body: The National Bureau of Statistics said headline inflation fell to 14.63 percent in September 2026, from 15.39 percent in August, continuing a downward trend. Food inflation was 19.59 percent and core inflation, which excludes farm produce and energy, was 12.95 percent. Urban inflation was 15.64 percent and rural inflation 12.46 percent.
stories.why: Inflation is one of the most common economy questions in Nigerian exams and interviews.

cards.front: What was Nigeria's headline inflation rate in September 2026 (NBS)?
cards.back: 14.63 percent, down from 15.39 percent in August.

stories.title: Troops clear camps and arrest suspected gunrunner in Plateau
stories.body: The military said troops of Operation Enduring Peace and 33 Artillery Brigade cleared suspected terrorist camps in Dajin Madam Forest, across Kanam and Wase LGAs, and killed two suspects near Kukawa village. A suspected gunrunner was arrested with an AK-47 at Gindiri Market in Mangu LGA. The details come from a military statement and were not independently verified.
stories.why: Arms trafficking keeps the North-central's farmer-herder and bandit violence going.

cards.front: Which military operation covers Plateau State?

stories.title: Herzog asks Eisenkot to form Israel's next government
stories.body: President Isaac Herzog tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government after the 27 October election. Eisenkot's alliance won 48 seats and Netanyahu's bloc 53, both short of 61. Eisenkot has six weeks and said he is open to including Netanyahu. He has ruled out relying on Arab-led parties, which won a record 19 seats. Netanyahu stays caretaker prime minister.
stories.why: A change of Israeli government could affect the Gaza ceasefire and the war with Iran.

cards.front: Who was asked to form Israel's government in November 2026?
cards.back: Gadi Eisenkot, given six weeks by President Herzog.
